WSJ: United Airlines will stop personal AI agents from booking tickets on its systems, warning they could leak sensitive data or make unintended purchases.

will let AI agents read its flight options and prices but will block them from completing any purchase on its website.
virals.draft_en:
The WSJ reports that United Airlines will no longer let personal AI agents book tickets through its systems. The stated risk: they could leak sensitive data, or complete purchases nobody meant to make.

Those agents may still look up flight options and prices. What gets blocked is finishing a purchase on the airline website.

articles.title: The 'SaaS is dead' posts are not arguing about the same product
articles.thesis: Today's outsider sample used the same slogan to mean three different things: a eulogy, a request to leave the timeline, and a UX complaint.
outline: The three hooks as they appeared, with their view counts
What each post actually claims, without adding a fourth claim
Why a slogan this short keeps getting reused
How to read the next 'SaaS is dead' post before agreeing with it

articles.title: When an indie hacker complaint is actually a traction report
articles.thesis: The truncated 'stupid indie hacker problems' list is mostly what happens after too many people show up: notifications, a server upgrade, and customer questions.
outline: The four visible items, including the line that cuts off
Why notification and server pressure show up together
What the list does not say, because the source was truncated
A short checklist for telling a complaint from a traction tell
articles.visual: Cover: four stacked cards matching the visible list items. Inline: a still of the truncated last line.
articles.why: Outsider @eliana_jordan reached 4,334 views with a truncated indie hacker problems list, and @codevsdev's related image reached 13,056 views.

x_keywords.method: Read-only x MCP search_posts_all, 2 calls per keyword: last 24 h and previous 24 h (24-48 h ago); lang:en, no retweets/replies, sort=relevancy, up to 25 posts per window. This is a SAMPLE of top-relevance posts, not every post on X. Views = impression_count at fetch time. Rank = sum of sampled 24 h views; 48 h = both windows; trend = 24 h sum / previous 24 h sum (up >=1.3, down <=0.7). Fresh posts are still gaining views, so 'up' is understated. Top-post share > 70% means one viral post carries the keyword.

trend_radar.legend: Trend match 0-100% = 1 - prod(1 - w) over matched 24 h keywords that another author also used in the 48 h window (w: rank 1-10 0.35, 11-25 0.22, 26-40 0.12, curated 0.20). Verdict: >= 50% -> trend; else video/image in the post data -> visual; else >= 100K followers (outsiders without follower data: >= 500K views, estimate) -> author/audience; else coincidence/other. Missing data shows as 'no data'. Heat = sum log10(views) of topic posts (24 h x1, 24-48 h x0.5), scaled to 100. Momentum = log-views last 24 h / previous 24 h. Trend-input-only accounts feed the corpus but are never shown as hits.
